data.narrative:
Maritime Fusion, a Seed-stage company in the Climate & Energy sector co-founded by Justin Cohen and Jason Kaufmann, has raised $4.5M to date. The valuation universe comprises 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though peers span a range of maturities and business models within the broader energy-transition space.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using the $4.5M in total raised as a proxy for current value, a typical 2.5x multiplier applied to Seed-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $11.3M. A Peer-Median approach could not be applied: while 8 same-sector peers exist (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix), none met the narrow filters of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables—requiring at least three datapoints for statistical reliability. Extrapolating from broader sector medians would risk obscuring Maritime Fusion's specific characteristics.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $9.6M (low) to $12.9M (high), with a median of $11M. This range reflects the limited methodological foundation: reliance on a single step-up model introduces sensitivity to multiplier assumptions. Key uncertainties include the sustainability of the 2.5x advancement multiplier for this particular frontier-tech sub-sector and the absence of validated peer comparables at equivalent stage and scale. A peer-based validation would materially strengthen confidence once sufficient same-stage datapoints materialize.
